newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firm on low U.S. long bond yield.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firm on low U.S. long bond yield.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed sharply firmer on Friday after dealers sold long dollar positions after unexpected strength on the U.S. bond market, traders said.
"Those who were long on dollars squared positions this morning, and from then on the market practically stood still," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate ended 4.2 and 3.5 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.9070/7.9100 and 7.9040/7.9070 per dollar.
Same-day peso contracts closed earlier 2.9 centavos firmer at 7.8990/7.9030 per dollar.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was up 11/32 to yield 6.89 percent as the foreign exchange markets were closing in Mexico.

Dealers said market activity was subdued as many in Mexico had taken a long weekend's vacation between public holidays celebrated on Thursday, May 1, for Labor Day and the anniversary of the battle of Puebla on Monday, May 5.
Traders saw the peso weakening against the dollar when dealing resumes next Tuesday, due to forecast cuts in primary interest rates at the central bank's weekly auction of government securities.
"Next week's auction will be very important; they could well cut rates and push the peso down against the dollar," a trader said.
